title: Slow-book rebuild
hypothesis: Vol-targeted momentum plus PEAD and a capped reversion leg make a viable S&P book.
question: With the accounting fixed, could a slower book (momentum, PEAD, pairs, reversion capped at 15%) clear Sharpe 0.6 with drawdown above −25%?
prior: Cross-sectional momentum (Jegadeesh and Titman 1993) is the strongest single-stock anomaly on record.
citations: Jegadeesh, N. & Titman, S. (1993). Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers. JF 48(1).
method: Window extended to 2000 →; risk-parity blend with a Sharpe tilt, weights lagged one day.
Promotion rules fixed in advance (momentum > 0.5, PEAD > 0.4, combined > 0.6).
verdict_reason: The v27 audit found momentum's +0.54 came from five corrupted 2010–2011 price days, and PEAD's edge came from mixing cached closes with freshly downloaded opens. Once fixed (v28), both collapsed.
lessons: Sanitise bad ticks before trusting any single-stock backtest.
Never mix data vintages inside one run.
footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
